q.t: Which of these is an irrational number?
q.e: √2 = 1.41421… never ends and never repeats, so it cannot be written as p/q. √4 = 2 is rational.
√9 = 3 = 3/1. A root is irrational only when it does not come out exactly.
1/3 = 0.333… The 3 repeats for ever. Every rational number either terminates or repeats.
The real numbers are all the rationals and all the irrationals together.
Same base, so add the exponents: 2⁵ = 32.
π = 3.14159… never ends or repeats. 22/7 is only a handy approximation.

q.t: Write 0.25 in the form p/q in lowest terms.

q.e: 4 + 3 = 7. (It is not √25 — roots cannot be added under one sign.)
The power 1/3 means the cube root: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

q.t: How many rational numbers lie between any two different rational numbers?
q.e: Their average lies between them, and you can keep averaging again and again without end.

q.t: Write 0.333… (3 repeating) in the form p/q.

q.e: Multiply top and bottom by √2: √2/(√2 × √2) = √2/2. The value is unchanged because √2/√2 = 1.
Squaring undoes the square root.
Cube root first (3), then square: 9.
They are like terms — 3 lots of √2 and 5 lots of √2 make 8 lots.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875. It terminates because 8 = 2³ has no prime factor other than 2 or 5.
(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² = 25 − 2. The roots cancel.
Fourth root of 16 is 2; 2³ = 8.

q.t: Which of these is a rational number?
q.e: (√5)² = 5. The others still contain √5, so they stay irrational.

q.t: Write 0.4777… (only the 7 repeating) in the form p/q.

q.e: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate √3 + √2. The bottom becomes 3 − 2 = 1.

q.t: Write 1.272727… (27 repeating) in the form p/q.

q.e: The negative power flips the fraction: (125/64)^(2/3). Cube roots give 5/4, and squaring gives 25/16.
Multiply by (2 − √3)/(2 − √3). The bottom is 4 − 3 = 1.
Add the exponents: 2/3 + 1/3 = 1, so the answer is 2¹.

q.t: Which of these rational numbers lies between √2 and √3?
q.e: √2 ≈ 1.414 and √3 ≈ 1.732. Only 1.5 is between them.
Flip: (16/81)^(3/4). Fourth roots give 2/3, and cubing gives 8/27.
1/x = 1/(3 + 2√2) = 3 − 2√2 (the denominator becomes 9 − 8 = 1). Adding, the roots cancel: 6.
1/x = 2 − √3, so x + 1/x = 4. Squaring: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 16.
Multiply top and bottom by (√5 − √3): (5 + 3 − 2√15)/(5 − 3) = 4 − √15. So a = 4 and b = 1.

q.t: Write 0.2353535… (35 repeating) in the form p/q.

q.e: 2 + 3 = 5; 5³ = 125; 5 × 125 = 625; the fourth root of 625 is 5.
Rationalising each gives (√2 − 1) + (√3 − √2) + (√4 − √3). The middle terms cancel, leaving √4 − 1 = 1.
(1 + √2)² = 1 + 2√2 + 2 = 3 + 2√2, so the square root is 1 + √2.
Let each equal k. Then 2 = k^(1/x), 3 = k^(1/y) and 6 = k^(−1/z). Since 2 × 3 = 6, 1/x + 1/y = −1/z.
The exponents are (a² − b²) + (b² − c²) + (c² − a²) = 0, and x⁰ = 1.
